newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan to meet Israeli foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan to meet Israeli foreign minister.

text.p: The office of Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Monday he would meet Israel's foreign minister when he visits Ankara this week after earlier expectations that no meeting would occur.
"Yes it is true, they will meet tommorrow evening," a spokesman for Erbakan told Reuters. A prime ministry statement said the two would meet at 7.00 p.m. (1600 GMT).

Israel's ambassador Zvi Elpeleg said earlier Erbakan had ignored repeated requests for a meeting with Istraeli Foreign Minister David Levy, who begins on Tuesday a two-day visit aimed at strengthening ties sought by Turkey's secularist generals.

Israel had quickly distanced itself from the comments, saying the itinerary was up to Turkey. "The ambassador was never instructed to ask for the meeting and if he did, it was done without Levy's knowledge," said an official in Jerusalem.
Levy is also to meet President Suleyman Demirel, Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller and other ministers from her secularist wing of the coalition. He later travels to Istanbul to meet Jewish leaders.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, won a slim plurality in general polls in 1995 after a campaign that included promises to renounce a training pact with Israel signed by the Turkish army's number two.
